chat.a: Net sales were £1.01M in week 32, −1.6% vs last year. Knitwear is the drag at −22.3%, or −£65K; everything else is +6.7%.

Every knitwear family is down, the Cloud Crew most at −28.0%. Stock has not slowed down with sales: it has 22.4 weeks of supply, against a 14-week ceiling. I'd hold the next delivery and plan a markdown.
Two different stories. Stores are −11.5% vs last year, while online is +15.0%. Online is now 35% of sales.
Outerwear. The Field Jacket is +10.2% vs last year and outerwear overall is +23.0%.

chat.q: Where are new customers coming from?
chat.a: More and more from online. New customers there are +46.0% vs last year, while stores are −20.5%. Online now brings in 43% of new customers, and 30% of them are Gen Z, against 17% in stores.

insights.headline: Knitwear and stores are pulling the week down — Knitwear is −22.3% and Cloud Crew stock is piling up, while Outerwear and Online grow.
insights.deck: Net sales were £1.01M, −1.6% vs LY — a little better than −2.5% over the prior four weeks. Knitwear is the biggest drag at −6.4 pts; Outerwear offsets +4.6 pts. By channel the week splits in two: Stores −11.5%, Online +15.0%.
insights.why: Knitwear is the story: all three families are down, led by Cloud Crew at −28.0% (−3.7 pts), and it isn't one week — Knitwear was −20.9% over the prior four weeks too. Outerwear holds up, with Field Jacket +10.2% and the new Harbor Parka adding +3.1 pts. Stores take −6.4 pts while Online adds +4.5 pts, up from +9.2% over the prior four weeks.

actions.b: 22.4 weeks of cover against a 14-week ceiling, with units −27.7% vs LY. About 10,230 units sit above the 14-week ceiling, and 17,520 above the 8-week target.

actions.t: Test a markdown on Fisherman Cardigan before it follows.
actions.b: 17.9 weeks of cover, also over the 14-week ceiling, with sales −16.7% vs LY.

actions.t: Test more Online spend before moving budget.
actions.b: Online is +15.0% vs LY, up from +9.2% over the prior four weeks, and now brings 35% of sales. Growth alone doesn't show what extra spend would add — a holdout test does, before the next pound moves.

insights.bottom: Knitwear is down while Outerwear is up, so a mild autumn is a hypothesis to check against regional weather, not the explanation. The stores gap is the bigger question: if Online keeps taking share, the store plan needs rethinking, not waiting out.

drills.q: What would the week look like without Knitwear?
drills.b: £784K against £734K last year. The rest of the range is growing; Knitwear alone turns the week negative.

drills.q: Is knitwear a price problem or a demand problem?
drills.t: Demand — fewer units at a steady price.
drills.b: Cloud Crew units are −27.7% vs LY with average price −0.5% (£77.34 vs £77.71). Shoppers are buying fewer jumpers, not cheaper ones.
Stores are −11.5% against −9.5% over the prior four weeks. Concessions +2.1%, Online +15.0%.

review.headline: Most friction this week is about time periods and definitions, not wrong numbers.
review.text: Buyers asked 96 questions. Only 1 answer had a number the checker flagged; the bigger theme is 5 questions where “October” or “last month” was read as the last 4 weeks. One theme needs a business definition before anyone can fix it.
